title: Contact and Protocol
premise: Jude Blackwood, a hostage negotiator whose one failed case still haunts them, has spent years living under a carefully constructed false identity—until a calendar invitation arrives from a handler who died six months ago, summoning them to a dead drop with proof that the failure was engineered. The evidence implicates a covert tri-national program that sacrifices negotiators to protect its operations, and the assassin sent to erase Jude is the same person they once talked off a rooftop. As three governments close in and the assassin's loyalty fractures, Jude must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the one person their lie was built to shield. In the end, Jude trades their own freedom for the release of the program's files, walking into custody with the truth already loose in the world.
about_author: Wendell Dunmore is a former crisis-line counselor who spent a decade listening to people at the edge before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about the quiet machinery of institutions and the people who get caught in its gears.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Living quietly as a logistics consultant, Jude receives a meeting invite from their dead handler, Mara Voss, scheduled for tomorrow. The go-bag by the door suddenly feels less like paranoia than prophecy. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve—the past has found a door back in.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. At an abandoned rail depot, Jude finds no body but a burner phone loaded with encrypted files and a warning: 'They let her fail you on purpose.' A watcher in the shadows forces Jude to run. Emotional beat: vertigo—the foundation of Jude's new life cracking open.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jude and Agent Reyes (US liaison). The file fragments name a joint program called LANTERN across American, British, and French intelligence. Reyes is ordered to find and silence the leak—unaware of what she's silencing. Emotional beat: the machinery of power grinding awake, indifferent to individuals.

chapters.title: The Rooftop Ghost
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jude and the assassin, Elias Wren. Wren, the man Jude once talked down from a ledge years ago, is assigned the kill. He recognizes his old negotiator mid-surveillance and hesitates for the first time in his career. Emotional beat: recognition as wound—two people bound by a moment neither can forget.

chapters.title: What the Lie Was For
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Flashbacks interleave with the present as Jude decodes Voss's files, revealing the failed negotiation was staged to bury LANTERN's existence—and that Voss died trying to make amends. Jude's hidden daughter, protected by the false identity, becomes leverage. Emotional beat: guilt transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Paris, After Midnight
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jude and Reyes. Jude meets a French archivist who confirms LANTERN's reach, then narrowly escapes a coordinated sweep. Reyes, tracking the same trail, begins doubting her orders. Emotional beat: pursuit tightening; allies and hunters converging on the same dark corridor.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: POV: Jude and Wren, face to face at last. Instead of killing Jude, Wren demands the truth he was never given about his own recruitment. They strike an uneasy bargain: Wren will delay his handlers while Jude reaches the one journalist Voss trusted. Emotional beat: love against duty—loyalty bending toward the human over the institution.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: POV: all three threads converge. The handoff to the journalist goes wrong; Reyes catches Jude, Wren takes a bullet covering the escape, and LANTERN's director offers Jude erasure of their past in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: climax of pressure—every price itemized, every escape route closing.

chapters.title: Negotiation
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. In the program's own safehouse, Jude does the only thing they know how to do: negotiate. Using Voss's complete files as collateral, Jude forces Reyes to choose between complicity and conscience, buying time for the upload to finish. Emotional beat: the negotiator's art turned on the powerful—words as weapons.

chapters.title: What Survives
chapters.summary: POV: Jude, coda from Reyes. The files publish worldwide; LANTERN scatters but survives in shadow. Jude surrenders voluntarily, trading testimony for their daughter's continued anonymity, while Reyes resigns to carry the story forward. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—the price of survival paid in full, and worth it.
